prompt:
I need the front end for Hearthchart. A household health-records app where parents keep each family member's immunizations, allergies, medications and doctor details and reuse them to fill out school, camp and sports forms.

Who's using it: Darnell, a father of three who works as a regional bus dispatcher and handles the kids' paperwork. He isn't medically trained and relies on the pediatrician's printouts to get dates and doses right.

What they're doing right now: It's Thursday evening and the health form for his 11-year-old daughter Imani's winter sleepaway camp is due Friday at noon. Most of it filled in from what's already stored, but the app has flagged three problems: her Tdap booster date comes before her 11th birthday, which the camp's rules won't accept; her EpiPen expiration date has passed; and her daily cetirizine dose is entered as '10' with no unit. He has the pediatrician's after-visit summary photo on hand and needs to fix each one, add the camp's required emergency contact who isn't a parent, and sign off on the form before submitting it.

What's in the system at this point: Household of five: Darnell, his partner Keisha, Imani (born 2015-03-08), Malik (8) and Zuri (3). Imani's record holds 19 immunization entries (e.g. Tdap stored as 2025-11-20, but the after-visit summary says 2026-04-02; MMR doses 2016 and 2019), allergies (tree nuts, severe; amoxicillin, rash), medications (cetirizine 10 mg daily; epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg, lot expired 2026-09), pediatrician Dr. Anika Sorensen at Eastgate Pediatrics, and insurance member ID. The camp form for Camp Ridgeline Winter Session (Dec 27–Jan 2) has 6 sections and 48 fields: 41 filled from stored data, 4 needing review, 3 empty, including a non-parent emergency contact, last tetanus date and a physician signature date within the past 12 months.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
